title: MPI Progress For All
problem: MPI progress semantics are poorly defined, limiting effective computation-communication overlap and preventing integration with modern programming paradigms. This opacity hinders explicit performance optimization and user-space MPI extension.
motivation: High-performance computing requires well-defined MPI progress mechanisms to enable efficient overlap, support contemporary runtimes like task-based systems, and allow user-space functionality extensions.
method: The authors reverse-engineered how MPI (Message Passing Interface—a standard for programs to send messages to each other) actually decides when to check for incoming messages and process them. They mapped out common patterns in how programs handle asynchronous communication (messages arriving at unpredictable times), and pinpointed which parts of the system create performance bottlenecks. They then designed new MPI features that let programmers write custom code to manage message checking themselves, instead of being locked into MPI's hidden, one-size-fits-all approach.
key_novelty: MPI extensions enable users to explicitly construct and manage progress engines (systems that decide when the program checks for incoming messages), replacing reliance on MPI's built-in opaque mechanisms.
contributions: Analysis of MPI progress implementation and asynchronous communication patterns
Identification of key factors influencing computation-communication overlap performance
Set of MPI extensions for explicit user-space progress engine management
Comparison demonstrating reduced complexity versus previous MPI approaches
